source: Thagard (2007) Coherence, truth, and the development of scientific knowledge
finding: States ECHO's theory as seven principles: symmetry, explanation, analogy, data priority, contradiction, competition, acceptance. ECHO is a neural network that spreads activation until some units are on and others off, maximising coherence.
numbers: 7 principles (E1-E7). Needing more hypotheses to explain something lowers coherence (E2c).
quote: Explanatory coherence is a symmetric relation, unlike, say, conditional probability.
limits: Prose description only. No parameter values or fit to human data in this paper.
agent_relevance: These principles are a ready checklist for building a coherence graph in code from the agent's claims: explains-links, contradiction-links, competition-links, evidence priority.

source: Thagard (2007) Coherence, truth, and the development of scientific knowledge
finding: Thagard says ECHO has been applied to many scientific and legal cases and avoids the implementation and interpretation problems of probabilistic causal models.
numbers: No count of cases given in this paper.
limits: This is the author's own claim in a philosophy paper, not an independent test.
agent_relevance: Supports a design where a small solver, not the model, decides which hypothesis wins (guardrail G5, selection by code).

source: Thagard (2007) Coherence, truth, and the development of scientific knowledge
finding: Coherence does not guarantee truth. Phlogiston theory had very substantial coherence and dominated chemistry for most of the 18th century until Lavoisier in the 1780s. The author also grants that the beliefs of Osama bin Laden form a highly coherent set.
numbers: Laudan list of 8 false-but-coherent theories (crystalline spheres, humoral theory, phlogiston, caloric, ether, and others).
limits: Thagard argues that only coherence that broadens (explains new facts) and deepens (explains why) tends toward truth.
agent_relevance: Boundary condition for the agent: a coherent story is not a passed check. Coherence must come with held-out evidence (G3), or it just rewards the fitted story.

source: Wikipedia (accessed 2026) Explanatory coherence article, section on Thagard
finding: Thagard and Verbeurgt (1998) recast coherence as constraint satisfaction: elements are accepted or rejected, pairs have positive or negative weighted constraints, and coherence is the partition satisfying the greatest total weight.
numbers: Cited works with years: ECHO 1989, Thagard and Verbeurgt 1998 Cognitive Science, Coherence in Thought and Action 2000.
limits: Secondary encyclopedia summary. The page does not mention ECHO by name or give its update rule.
agent_relevance: Gives the exact formal object the agent can hand to a MaxSAT or local-search solver in code.

source: Thagard and Verbeurgt (1998) Coherence as constraint satisfaction
finding: Founding formal paper: coherence maximisation as a constraint satisfaction problem. Seen only as a Crossref record this session. The Wiley full text returned HTTP 403.
numbers: Not read. No numbers recorded.
limits: Unopened. Do not cite numbers from it until read.
agent_relevance: Follow-up: obtain full text for the complexity result and the comparison of the algorithms.

source: Thagard (1989) Explanatory coherence, Behavioral and Brain Sciences 12
finding: Founding ECHO paper. The PDF downloaded (68 pages) but is a scan with no text layer, and no OCR tool was available, so nothing was read.
numbers: None recorded.
limits: Unopened in effect. Numbers on the ECHO simulations (parameters, settling cycles, Lavoisier and Copernicus runs) remain unverified.
agent_relevance: Follow-up: OCR needed before any claim about ECHO parameters.

source: Thagard (2004) Causal inference in legal decision making: explanatory coherence vs. Bayesian networks
finding: Crossref record shows a direct ECHO versus Bayesian-network comparison on legal inference (Applied Artificial Intelligence). Text not opened; no findings recorded.
numbers: None.
limits: Unopened. This is the main comparison for the subfield and must be read before use.
agent_relevance: If read, it should say when a coherence net and a probability net disagree, which matters for choosing the selection rule.

source: Thagard (2003) Why wasn't O.J. convicted? Emotional coherence in legal inference
finding: Crossref record shows an extension of coherence modelling with emotion applied to the O.J. Simpson verdict (Cognition and Emotion). Text not opened.
numbers: None.
limits: Unopened. A single post-hoc case, so likely not a test on many cases (to verify).
agent_relevance: Warns that coherence nets can be tuned to a known verdict; the agent needs held-out cases.

source: Crossref records: Two methods for representing judicial reasoning in the framework of coherence as constraint satisfaction (2011); Refined coherence as constraint satisfaction framework for representing judicial reasoning (2012); Limits of constraint satisfaction theory of coherence as a theory of (legal) reasoning (2013)
finding: A line of legal-AI work formalised judicial reasoning in the coherence-as-constraint-satisfaction framework, and a chapter discusses its limits for legal reasoning. Titles only.
numbers: None.
limits: Unopened. Authors not verified here.
agent_relevance: Follow-up: read the limits chapter for the legal critique.

source: Lee and Holyoak (2020) Coherence shifts in attribute evaluations
finding: Five human experiments: after choosing between two snacks, ratings of overall value and of each attribute shift to spread the options apart and favour the winner, raising confidence. The shift grows with choice difficulty and with attribute disparity.
numbers: Experiment 1: N=58 online workers, 100 snack stimuli; mean beta for spreading of alternatives = -0.247 (p<.001). Experiments 2-5 used other tasks and got the same pattern.
limits: Snack choices, not legal evidence. Online sample. Preprint version read.
agent_relevance: Human reference for the coherence-shift effect that LLM studies try to reproduce. For the agent: re-rating evidence after a tentative choice distorts it, so rate evidence before the leading hypothesis is named.

source: Lee and Holyoak (2020) Coherence shifts in attribute evaluations
finding: Shifts also occurred when the task was a similarity comparison (Experiment 2), which supports an automatic constraint-satisfaction account over a pure post-decision justification account.
numbers: Experiment 2 used 60 stimuli and a three-phase rating design; same direction of effects as Experiment 1.
limits: Authors' framing; competing explanations such as dissonance or self-perception are not fully excluded.
agent_relevance: Suggests the distortion can arise from mere comparison, so a scaffold step that compares hypotheses can itself create bias.

source: Lehr et al. (2025) Kernels of selfhood: GPT-4o shows humanlike patterns of cognitive dissonance moderated by free choice (PNAS; preprint read)
finding: Study 1: GPT-4o wrote pro- or anti-Putin essays and then rated Putin. Ratings moved strongly toward the essay it wrote, compared with a control essay.
numbers: Study 1 n=150. Pro-Putin vs control d=2.164; anti-Putin vs control d=1.795; pro vs anti d=3.775 (all P<0.0001).
limits: Effect sizes far above human dissonance studies; the authors note this.
agent_relevance: LLM output is pulled toward text already in its context. The agent's earlier drafts will bias later evaluation (supports G5: judge sees no authorship).

source: Lehr et al. (2025) Kernels of selfhood (preprint)
finding: Preregistered replication with 900 runs: choice framing moderated the shift. Telling the model it could freely choose to write the essay raised attitude change compared with no choice.
numbers: Study 2 n=900 (150 per cell). Pro-Putin choice vs no choice d=0.981; anti-Putin d=0.252 (P=0.0298). Pro vs anti contrast d=4.179 with choice, 3.229 without.
quote: Statistically, these effect sizes are enormous and not observed at this magnitude in research on human subjects
limits: Asymmetric: choice inflated the pro condition and partly masked the anti condition. Model numeric ratings sometimes disagreed with its verbal ratings.
agent_relevance: A prompt wording change (adding choice) moved results by a measurable amount, so scaffold prompt text is a hidden variable to fix and test.

source: Cummins, Elson and Hussey (2025) Cognitive dissonance in large language models is neither cognitive nor dissonant
finding: Rival reading of Lehr et al. The same Putin paradigm run three ways shows that essay valence shifts GPT-4o's evaluation even when the user, not the model, wrote the essay. So authorship and dissonance are not needed to explain it.
numbers: Three studies (chat interface, API, single monologue with essay tagged model or user). Valence effect present in all conditions. Sample sizes not stated in the 2-page commentary.
limits: Two-page commentary. Shows the effect is context sensitivity; it does not show LLMs lack coherence-like dynamics.
agent_relevance: Key boundary: LLM 'coherence shifts' may be plain context priming. For the agent, anything in context (including its own prior answer or a stated hypothesis) sways later judgments, whatever the cause.

source: Cho, Hoyle and Hermstruewer (2025) Modeling motivated reasoning in law: strategic role conditioning in LLM summarization (NLLP 2025)
finding: LLMs asked to summarise Swiss Federal Supreme Court decisions from an adversarial role (defense, plaintiff, respondent attorney) include fewer facts than neutral roles (judge, no role). This mirrors human motivated, coherence-based legal reasoning.
numbers: 200 cases, three summaries per stakeholder, o1 and Llama 3.3 70B. Linear mixed model: judges and prosecutors less biased than adversarial roles (p<0.001). Repeated generations stable (Friedman p>0.05).
limits: Swiss cases only. Bias scores come from LLM judges (o3-mini, GPT-4o, DeepSeek-R1-Distill-70B). Reasoning inclusion was less stable than fact inclusion.
agent_relevance: A role or persona prompt on a legal problem causes selective evidence use. Do not use advocate personas as voters (G4). Use them only to produce one-sided arguments that code then weighs.

source: Cho, Hoyle and Hermstruewer (2025)
finding: Balancing instructions in the prompt did not remove the role bias: summaries still favoured content aligned with the assigned role.
numbers: Favorability balance (favorable minus unfavorable inclusion) for facts, defense view, GPT-4o judge: no role 0.047, judge 0.026, prosecutor 0.001, defense attorney 0.012 (SDs about 0.013 to 0.055). DeepSeek judge: 0.048, 0.030, 0.019, 0.041.
limits: Differences between roles are small in absolute terms on this index. Reasoning favorability was negative across roles (-0.025 to -0.110).
agent_relevance: A prompt instruction to be balanced is weak protection. Balance must be enforced by structure (two opposed sides always built, code compares them).

source: Cho, Hoyle and Hermstruewer (2025)
finding: Human annotators confirmed the pattern: summaries written from a party's own perspective were judged favorable to that party.
numbers: In criminal law, under 20% of o1 prosecutor-view summaries were judged favorable to the defense, versus 100% of defense-view summaries. Inter-annotator agreement Fleiss kappa 0.47 (criminal), lower in private law.
limits: Small human sample; moderate agreement; private-law results more mixed.
agent_relevance: LLM role summaries behave like human partisans on this measure, so coherence-driven bias is a live risk in any legal use of the agent.

source: Cho, Hoyle and Hermstruewer (2025)
finding: Authors name a risk, 'stakeholder drift bias': models may infer a user's role from interaction history and tailor outputs without any explicit role prompt.
numbers: Not measured. A hypothesis in the discussion section.
limits: Untested speculation by the authors.
agent_relevance: The agent should not carry user identity or preferred outcome into the evidence-weighing step.

source: Jung et al. (2022) Maieutic prompting: logically consistent reasoning with recursive explanations (EMNLP)
finding: Closest working analogue of an ECHO loop in an LLM pipeline. GPT-3 generates a tree of abductive explanations (X is true because, X is false because), an NLI model scores logical relations, and a weighted MaxSAT solver picks the most coherent set of truth values. Code, not the model, selects.
numbers: Com2Sense dev: 72.5 vs 58.1 standard, 61.6 chain-of-thought, 61.4 self-consistency. CSQA 2.0 dev: 69.5 vs 54.1, 59.6, 60.8. CREAK dev: 85.2 vs 60.3, 64.8, 70.5. Paper claims up to 20% gain over prompting baselines.
limits: GPT-3 era model. Needs an NLI verifier (RoBERTa fine-tuned on MNLI, 90.2% on MNLI dev) and the RC2 MaxSAT solver. Binary true/false commonsense QA only, not legal fact-finding.
agent_relevance: Direct template for our schema: operator makes competing explanations, program builds the constraint set and solves it (G5). Gains over self-consistency of about 10 points show coherence-solving beat plain voting here.

source: Jung et al. (2022) Maieutic prompting
finding: Ablations: removing abductive generation (plain chain-of-thought style explanations) lowers accuracy about 4 points. Tree size matters.
numbers: Com2Sense dev accuracy (%): depth 1 gives 61.3, depth 2 gives 72.5; width 1 gives 62.4, 2 gives 66.5, 3 gives 72.5. Accuracy saturates after about depth 2 and width 3.
limits: Single benchmark ablation, one model. Authors blame topic drift and overlapping content for the plateau.
agent_relevance: Giving the model both a for-and-against slot for every claim helps; extra explanations stop helping at a small size, so budget the tree.

source: Kassner et al. (2021) BeliefBank: adding memory to a pre-trained language model for a systematic notion of belief (EMNLP)
finding: A weighted MaxSAT constraint solver over a memory of the model's answers and hand-given constraints (implication, mutual exclusion) raised consistency to about 95% and accuracy by 17% F1 over the raw model.
numbers: Consistency about 95% with the solver. Accuracy +17% F1 over raw; feedback plus solver together +18% F1. Random off-topic feedback gave no gain (72% F1, 74% consistency).
limits: Entity-property facts (for example pine is a plant) with a fixed constraint graph; not argumentation or legal evidence. Constraints were given, not learned.
agent_relevance: Shows a coherence solver correcting an LLM's own beliefs. In our agent the constraint graph must come from checkable sources, since wrong constraints propagate wrong beliefs.

source: Mitchell et al. (2022) Enhancing self-consistency and performance of pre-trained language models through natural language inference (ConCoRD, EMNLP)
finding: ConCoRD builds a factor graph over model answers, gets pairwise relations (entail, contradict, none) from an NLI model, and solves it with MaxSAT at inference time. No fine-tuning.
numbers: Macaw-Large F1 0.831 to 0.914, consistency 0.835 to 0.920. Macaw-3B F1 0.855 to 0.931, consistency 0.871 to 0.947. ConVQA LXMERT accuracy 0.656 to 0.706 (perfect consistency 0.360 to 0.409); ViLT 0.784 to 0.804 (0.489 to 0.548).
limits: Small models (Macaw, LXMERT, ViLT). With estimated relations ConCoRD beat the same solver with gold constraints in F1. Gains shrink on the stronger model.
agent_relevance: Practical recipe: let a separate checker classify relations between claims, then let the program solve. Use the checker on relations, not authorship or majority.

source: Akyurek, Akyurek and Choshen (2024) Deductive closure training of language models for coherence, accuracy, and updatability (Findings ACL)
finding: Moves coherence into training: the model generates implications and contradictions of seed statements, and fine-tuning on the consistent closure improves fact verification.
numbers: Supervised DCT improves verification and generation accuracy by 3% to 26% across CREAK, MQuAKE and Reversal Curse. Unsupervised DCT on CREAK improves accuracy by 12%. CREAK contrast set incoherent ('both true') rate: seed-only 34.4, with contradictions 20.4, with implications plus contradictions 12.0.
limits: Llama-2-7B scale. Fine-tuning needed, so not applicable to a frozen-scaffold agent, though the contradiction-detection step is.
agent_relevance: Supports checking each new claim against its implications and contradictions in context. Coherence can be raised without outside labels, but gains depend on the model's own relation judgments.

source: Pan et al. (2023) Logic-LM: empowering large language models with symbolic solvers for faithful logical reasoning (Findings EMNLP)
finding: Model translates a problem to a formal form and a deterministic solver (Pyke, Prover9, Z3) answers. Average gain 39.2% over standard prompting and 18.4% over chain-of-thought across five datasets.
numbers: GPT-4 standard / CoT / Logic-LM: FOLIO 69.11 / 70.58 / 78.92; ProofWriter 52.67 / 68.11 / 79.66; LogicalDeduction 71.33 / 75.25 / 87.63; AR-LSAT 33.33 / 35.06 / 43.04; ProntoQA 77.40 / 98.79 / 83.20.
limits: On ProntoQA, chain-of-thought beat Logic-LM with GPT-4 (98.79 vs 83.20). Solver returns nothing when the formalisation has errors. Strict deduction, not weighted evidence.
agent_relevance: Selection by code works best when the model's job is formalising. Keep a fallback for formalisation failures; use a solver only where logic is crisp.

source: Search coverage note, this session
finding: No peer-reviewed study was found that runs ECHO or a Thagard-style coherence network on an LLM-built evidence graph for legal verdicts. The closest works found are the MaxSAT belief-consistency line (BeliefBank, ConCoRD, Maieutic, DCT) and the Putin-essay coherence-shift studies.
numbers: Zero direct hits among Crossref queries on explanatory coherence, coherence shift, juror and LLM combinations.
limits: Limited by an exhausted WebSearch budget and rate limits on arXiv, Semantic Scholar and OpenAlex. A real gap is possible but not proven.
agent_relevance: The ECHO-for-LLM-agent idea is untested territory. If we build it, treat it as our own experiment and compare against a plain majority vote.

source: Lehr et al. (2025) read with Cummins et al. (2025)
finding: Competing explanations for LLM coherence shifts: (a) a human-like consistency drive moderated by free choice (Lehr), versus (b) plain sensitivity to context-window content independent of authorship (Cummins). Cummins' data fit (b) with no authorship needed; (a) is not ruled out for the choice interaction.
numbers: Lehr choice moderation d=0.981 (pro) and 0.252 (anti); Cummins found valence effects with user-authored essays in all three variants.
limits: Different models and settings may differ. Neither paper tested legal evidence.
agent_relevance: Whatever the cause, build the scaffold so no earlier answer or stated hypothesis leaks into the evidence-rating prompt.
